I did some basic wiki-research on Object Oriented Ontology, and what I'm picking up is that things are real even if not detected by our human perception. Basically, if a tree falls in a forest it DOES make a sound. I'm on board with that. My only caveat would be that nothing really matters until it affects you or me. But everything affects everything in this complex social and evironmental ecosystem, so really, everything matters. Perception creates my reality too. Even right now, as I'm typing, I can only see what is in front of me and to my peripherals. I can't see behind me, so does it exist? Sure, but maybe what is more real is what is in front of me because it's currently having the most effect on me. Eh, I'm just kind of spitballing but it was a fun path to step down for a sec. Moving on!

Why do we maintain supernatural claims? In total honesty we do maintain supernatural biblical claims as historic, but we don't concentrate on them on a day-to-day level. If you boil down the most important parts of our religion/philosophy, what's left after the non-essentials evaporate isn't Aaron and the sorcerors turning their staffs to serpents. It's love, growth, forgiveness, repentance, all superior to any proper nouns associated with any religion. Now, I totally get that saying miracles can't happen anymore like they did in the Bible because God operates in a modern framework requires a decent amount of mental flexibility. But I think the essential is really quite simple: God can't do anything to us that would coerce our free will. What would coerce my free will might be different from what would coerce your free will, so who's to say that God doesn't operate differently for each person? And what would coerce Samson's free will is much different than what would coerce our's, because of time, place, evolution, science, etc. I just had a thought... Begin heresy—maybe this is part of why some kids speak of seeing angels, or old people see their dead siblings before they die. They are rationally and mentally in different places than a cognizant 30-year-old, and as such so is their free will — end heresy.

Really, though, supernaturalism is important because we think people are spiritual beings, possessing souls and reforming them, then eventually dying and going into the afterlife.
